Unit 9: Computer Systems

SL curriculum overview and structured learning plan.

Introduction

What actually happens inside the box?

This unit peels back the layers of abstraction to reveal the physical reality of the Von Neumann Architecture. You will learn how the CPU orchestrates billions of operations per second using the Fetch-Decode-Execute cycle, and how memory hierarchies balance speed, cost, and capacity.

You'll start by mapping the internal topography of the CPU (Registers, ALU, CU). Then you'll trace the journey of a single instruction through the FDE Cycle, optimizing performance with Cache and Secondary Storage, before expanding to the global scale of Cloud Computing.

The CPU & Registers

The Central Processing Unit (CPU) is the brain. It contains specific components:

  • ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit): Does the math and logic checks.
  • CU (Control Unit): The conductor that directs data flow.
  • Registers: Tiny, super-fast storage slots (e.g., PC, MAR, MDR, ACC).
Memory Hierarchy

Not all memory is created equal. We balance speed vs size:

  1. Registers: Fastest, Tiny size.
  2. Cache (L1/L2/L3): Very fast, Small size.
  3. RAM (Primary): Fast, Medium size (Volatile).
  4. Storage (Secondary): Slow, Huge size (Non-volatile, e.g., SSD).
The FDE Cycle

The heartbeat of the computer. Millions of times a second, it follows these steps:

  • Fetch: Get the next instruction from RAM.
  • Decode: Figure out what it means.
  • Execute: Do it (e.g., Add numbers, Store data).
Cloud Computing

"The Cloud" is just someone else's computer. We abstract infrastructure using service models:

  • SaaS: Software as a Service (e.g., Google Docs).
  • PaaS: Platform as a Service (e.g., Heroku).
  • IaaS: Infrastructure as a Service (e.g., AWS EC2).
Key Terminology
TermDefinition
Von Neumann Architecture A design where data and instructions are stored in the same memory and accessed via buses.
Program Counter (PC) A register that holds the memory address of the NEXT instruction to be executed.
MAR (Memory Address Register) Holds the address of the memory location currently being accessed (read or written).
MDR (Memory Data Register) Holds the data that has just been fetched from, or is about to be written to, memory.
Accumulator (ACC) A register that holds the intermediate results of ALU calculations.
Cache Small, high-speed memory located near the CPU to store frequently used data.
Primary Memory (RAM) Volatile memory that holds the OS, programs, and data currently in use.
Secondary Storage Non-volatile storage (HDD/SSD) used to allow data to be persistent.
SaaS / PaaS / IaaS Service models for Cloud Computing (Software / Platform / Infrastructure as a Service).
